paragraphs: Fifth Third Bancorp (the "Bancorp" or "Fifth Third"), an Ohio corporation organized in 1975, is a bank holding company ("BHC") as defined by the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the "BHCA"), and has elected to be treated as a financial holding company ("FHC") under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999 ("GLBA") and regulations of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the "FRB").

The Bancorp is a diversified financial services company headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio and is the indirect holding company of Fifth Third Bank, National Association (the "Bank"). As of December 31, 2025, Fifth Third had $214 billion in assets and operates 1,130 full-service Banking Centers and 2,199 Fifth Third branded ATMs in Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana, Michigan, Illinois, Florida, Tennessee, West Virginia, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Alabama. The Bancorp operates three main businesses: Commercial Banking, Consumer and Small Business Banking and Wealth and Asset Management. The Bancorp's trust and registered investment advisory businesses had approximately $690 billion in total assets under care and managed $80 billion in assets for individuals, corporations and not-for-profit organizations as of December 31, 2025. Fifth Third's common stock is traded on the NASDAQ® Global Select Market under the symbol FITB.

The Bancorp's subsidiaries provide a wide range of financial products and services to the commercial, financial, retail, governmental, educational, energy and healthcare sectors. This includes a variety of checking, savings and money market accounts, wealth management solutions, payments and commerce solutions, securities products and services, insurance services and credit products such as commercial loans and leases, mortgage loans, credit cards, installment loans and other lending products. These products and services are delivered through a variety of channels including the Bancorp's banking centers, other offices, telephone sales, the internet and mobile applications. The Bank has deposit insurance provided by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC") through the Deposit Insurance Fund (the "DIF"). Refer to Exhibit 21 filed as an attachment to this Annual Report on Form 10-K for a list of subsidiaries of the Bancorp as of February 15, 2026.
Additional information regarding the Bancorp's businesses is included in Item 7 of this Annual Report.

The Bancorp, primarily through the Bank, competes for deposits, loans and other banking services in its principal geographic markets as well as in selected national markets as opportunities arise. In addition to banking institutions, the Bancorp competes with securities dealers, brokers, mortgage bankers, investment advisors, specialty finance, private credit, financial technology and insurance companies. These companies compete across geographic boundaries and provide customers with meaningful alternatives to traditional banking services in nearly all significant products. The increasingly competitive environment is primarily a result of changes in regulation, changes in technology, product delivery systems and the accelerating pace of consolidation among financial service providers. These competitive trends are likely to continue.

The Bancorp's human capital strategy is designed to attract, develop and retain talent. This strategy ensures that Fifth Third has the talent, capabilities and organizational structure to support business needs now and in the future. As of December 31, 2025, the Bancorp had 18,676 full-time equivalent employees, compared to 18,616 as of December 31, 2024. These employees support the organization's ambition and purpose by upholding its values by committing to excellence, being connected and acting with creativity and courage. Fifth Third is committed to living its values, serving its customers, delivering financial performance and being recognized as a leader in building an engaging workplace.

Fifth Third believes that an engaged workforce is one of its most valuable assets in sustaining its success. The Bancorp's continuous listening strategy is an important component of its inclusive culture and offers a holistic approach to collecting, measuring and responding to employee feedback through a variety of methods in order to enhance the employee experience at critical points along the employee lifecycle. At the foundation of the Bancorp's listening strategy is the Employee Viewpoints Survey, which includes questions related to engagement, inclusion, well-being, employee expectations and their intent to stay.

The Bancorp's learning, development and career mobility strategy delivers personalized and accessible experiences that fuel career growth and help retain talent. In response to employee feedback, Fifth Third continued its focus on career mobility with enhanced tools to support internal career pathing. This includes a robust suite of learning resources covering several areas, including leadership and professional development to foster learning and career advancement across the employee population. In 2025, employees engaged in over 550,000 hours of discretionary learning.

In 2025, Fifth Third launched a comprehensive platform designed to deliver leadership development content and experiences for leaders at all levels. Several new development offerings were launched, including generative Artificial Intelligence ("AI") training, coaching skills for managers and targeted programs to strengthen professional and leadership capabilities across the organization. Fifth Third leaders participated

in more than 3,200 distinct development experiences. The Bancorp's commitment to compliance and risk management remains strong, with employees and contingent workers completing over 450,000 course hours on these critical topics during 2025.
Total Rewards – Compensation and Benefits

The Bancorp understands the importance of rewarding employees for their talents and commitment to excellence. To reflect that, employees' Total Rewards package includes both competitive compensation as well as a complete benefits offering that supports employees through the stages of their careers and lives.

The Bancorp is committed to providing competitive compensation programs that attract and retain top talent, while driving the business strategy and effectively managing risk. Fifth Third's compensation programs are designed to reward performance and align with regulatory expectations while reflecting the Bancorp's values and behavioral standards. The Bancorp's compensation philosophy is centered on creating long-term shareholder value.

Fifth Third is committed to the holistic well-being of its employees. The benefits program is designed to address the personal and professional needs of employees and their families. In addition to traditional benefits offerings, the Bancorp provides comprehensive support with unique programs focused on the financial, physical, emotional and social well-being of employees.

paragraphs: The risks and uncertainties listed below present risks that could have a material impact on the Bancorp's business, financial condition or results of operations. Some of these risks and uncertainties are interrelated and the occurrence of one or more of them may exacerbate the effect of others. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones Fifth Third faces. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to Fifth Third or that Fifth Third currently believes to be immaterial may also adversely affect its business. Refer to page 19 for cautionary information regarding forward-looking statements.

When Fifth Third lends money or commits to lend money, the Bancorp incurs credit risk, or the risk of loss if borrowers do not repay their loans, leases, credit cards, derivative obligations or other credit obligations. The performance of these credit portfolios significantly affects the Bancorp's financial results and condition, including the level of credit losses and reserves for credit losses. Fifth Third's credit risk and credit losses can increase if its loans are concentrated among individual borrowers, borrowers engaged in the same or similar activities, industries or geographies, or to borrowers who as a group may be uniquely or disproportionately affected by economic or market conditions. Refer to the Credit Risk Management subsection of the Risk Management section in Item 7 of this Annual Report for more information on specific concentrations.

Fifth Third reserves for expected credit losses by establishing an allowance for credit losses through a charge to earnings. The amount of this allowance is based on Fifth Third's assessment of credit losses expected to be incurred in the credit portfolios, including unfunded commitments, and requires difficult, subjective and complex judgments about the environment, including analysis of economic or market conditions that may impair the ability of borrowers to repay their loans. Fifth Third may underestimate the credit losses expected to be incurred in its portfolios and have credit losses in excess of the amount reserved. Alternatively, Fifth Third may increase the reserve because of changing economic or market conditions, including inflation, interest rate fluctuations, higher unemployment, or other factors such as changing protections in credit agreements or changes in borrowers' behavior. Fifth Third believes that both the ALLL and reserve for unfunded commitments are adequate to cover expected losses at December 31, 2025. However there is no assurance that they will be sufficient to cover all potential future credit losses associated with exposures existing at December 31, 2025, especially if economic conditions decline.

Fifth Third has exposure to counterparties in the financial services industry and other industries and routinely executes transactions with such counterparties, which may expose Fifth Third to credit risk in the event of default of a counterparty or client. In addition, Fifth Third's credit risk may be affected when the collateral it holds cannot be realized or is liquidated at prices not sufficient to recover the full amount of the loan or derivative exposure. The commercial soundness of many financial institutions may be closely interrelated as a result of credit, trading, clearing or other relationships between the institutions. As a result, concerns about, or a default or threatened default by, one institution could lead to significant market-wide liquidity and credit problems, losses or defaults by other institutions. This is sometimes referred to as systemic risk and may adversely affect financial intermediaries, such as clearing agencies, clearing houses, banks, securities firms and exchanges, with which the Bancorp interacts on a daily basis, and therefore could adversely affect Fifth Third.

Some Fifth Third customers rely on additional sources of capital from outside the Bancorp. If public or private capital markets are disrupted or unavailable to these borrowers such that they cannot obtain funds for refinancing, those borrowers may experience a shortfall that would leave them unable to honor short-term and/or long-term obligations to the Bancorp.

Fifth Third must maintain adequate funding sources in the normal course of business to support its operations and fund outstanding liabilities, as well as meet regulatory expectations. Fifth Third primarily relies on bank deposits to be a low cost and stable source of funding for the loans it makes and the operation of its business. Core deposits, which include transaction deposits and certificates of deposit $250,000 or less, have historically provided Fifth Third with a sizeable source of relatively stable and low-cost funds (average core deposits funded 77% of average total assets for the year ended December 31, 2025). In addition to customer deposits, sources of liquidity include investments in the securities portfolio, Fifth Third's sale or securitization of loans in secondary markets, the pledging of loans and investment securities to access secured borrowing facilities through the FHLB and the FRB and Fifth Third's ability to raise funds in money markets and capital markets.

paragraphs: The following is Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations of certain significant factors that have affected Fifth Third Bancorp's (the "Bancorp" or "Fifth Third") financial condition and results of operations during the periods included in the Consolidated Financial Statements, which are a part of this filing. Reference to the Bancorp incorporates the parent holding company and all consolidated subsidiaries. The Bancorp's banking subsidiary is referred to as the Bank.

This overview of MD&A highlights selected information in the financial results of the Bancorp and may not contain all of the information that is important to you. For a more complete understanding of trends, events, commitments, uncertainties, liquidity, capital resources and critical accounting policies and estimates, you should carefully read this entire document. Each of these items could have an impact on the Bancorp's financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. In addition, refer to the Glossary of Abbreviations and Acronyms in this report for a list of terms included as a tool for the reader of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The abbreviations and acronyms identified therein are used throughout this MD&A, as well as the Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.

Net interest income, net interest margin, net interest rate spread and the efficiency ratio are presented in MD&A on an FTE basis. The FTE basis adjusts for the tax-favored status of income from certain loans and leases and securities held by the Bancorp that are not taxable for federal income tax purposes. The Bancorp believes this presentation to be the preferred industry measurement of net interest income as it provides a relevant comparison between taxable and non-taxable amounts. The FTE basis for presenting net interest income is a non-GAAP measure. For further information, refer to the Non-GAAP Financial Measures section of MD&A.

The Bancorp's revenues are dependent on both net interest income and noninterest income. For the year ended December 31, 2025, net interest income on an FTE basis and noninterest income provided 66% and 34% of total revenue, respectively. The Bancorp derives the majority of its revenues within the U.S. from customers domiciled in the U.S. Changes in interest rates, credit quality, economic trends and the capital markets are primary factors that drive the performance of the Bancorp. As discussed later in the Risk Management section of MD&A, risk identification, measurement, monitoring, control and reporting are important to the management of risk and to the financial performance and capital strength of the Bancorp.

Net interest income is the difference between interest income earned on assets such as loans, leases and securities, and interest expense incurred on liabilities such as deposits, other short-term borrowings and long-term debt. Net interest income is affected by the general level of interest rates, the relative level of short-term and long-term interest rates, changes in interest rates and changes in the amount and composition of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. Generally, the rates of interest the Bancorp earns on its assets and pays on its liabilities are established for a period of time. The change in market interest rates over time exposes the Bancorp to interest rate risk through potential adverse changes to net interest income and financial position. The Bancorp manages this risk by continually analyzing and adjusting the composition of its assets and liabilities based on their payment streams and interest rates, the timing of their maturities and their sensitivity to changes in market interest rates. Additionally, in the ordinary course of business, the Bancorp enters into certain derivative transactions as part of its overall strategy to manage its interest rate and prepayment risks. The Bancorp is also exposed to the risk of loss on its loan and lease portfolio as a result of changing expected cash flows caused by borrower credit events, such as loan defaults and inadequate collateral.

Noninterest income is derived from wealth and asset management revenue, commercial payments revenue, consumer banking revenue, capital markets fees, commercial banking revenue, mortgage banking net revenue, other noninterest income and net securities gains or losses. Noninterest expense includes compensation and benefits, technology and communications, net occupancy expense, equipment expense, loan and lease expense, marketing expense, card and processing expense and other noninterest expense.

On February 1, 2026, Fifth Third Bancorp closed the merger with Comerica Incorporated ("Comerica") in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $12.7 billion. Under the terms of the merger agreement, each outstanding share of Comerica's common stock was converted into the right to receive 1.8663 shares of Fifth Third Bancorp common stock and each outstanding share of Comerica's preferred stock was converted into the right to receive one share of a newly created series of preferred stock with comparable terms issued by the Bancorp.
Refer to Note 32 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for more information.

On September 30, 2025, the Bancorp redeemed all 14,000 outstanding shares of its 4.500% fixed-rate reset non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock, Series L, and the corresponding depositary shares, pursuant to its terms and conditions. Prior to the redemption, the dividend rate on the Series L preferred stock was set to reach its first dividend reset date at which time the dividend would have reset to the five-year U.S. Treasury rate plus 4.215%.

第五第三銀行控股公司（the "Bancorp" 或 "Fifth Third"），為一間於1975年成立於俄亥俄州的公司，為根據1956年銀行控股公司法案（the "BHCA"）所定義的銀行控股公司（"BHC"），並已選擇根據1999年格雷姆-李-布萊利法案（"GLBA"）及聯邦儲備銀行理事會（the "FRB"）的規則，被視為金融控股公司（"FHC"）。

第五第三銀行控股公司為一間多元化金融服務公司，總部設於俄亥俄州辛辛那提市，為第五第三銀行，國家協會（the "Bank"）的間接控股公司。截至2025年12月31日，第五第三銀行資產總額為2140億美元，並在俄亥俄州、肯塔基州、印第安納州、密歇根州、伊利諾州、佛羅裏達州、田納西州、西弗吉尼亞州、佐治亞州、北卡羅來納州、南卡羅來納州及阿拉巴馬州設有1,130間全功能銀行分行及2,199間第五第三品牌提款機。第五第三銀行控股公司主要經營三大業務：企業銀行、消費者及中小企業銀行及資產與財富管理。截至2025年12月31日，第五第三銀行控股公司的信託及註冊投資顧問業務總資產規模約為6900億美元，並為個人、公司及非營利機構管理約800億美元資產。第五第三銀行的普通股於NASDAQ® Global Select Market上市交易，代碼為FITB。

第五第三銀行控股公司的子公司為商業、金融、零售、政府、教育、能源及醫療等產業提供廣泛的金融產品與服務。此包括多種支票帳戶、儲蓄帳戶及貨幣市場帳戶、財富管理解決方案、支付與商業解決方案、證券產品與服務、保險服務及信貸產品，如商業貸款與租賃、房貸貸款、信用卡、分期貸款及其他貸款產品。這些產品與服務透過多種渠道提供，包括第五第三銀行控股公司的銀行分行、其他辦公室、電話銷售、互聯網及行動應用程式。第五第三銀行的存款由美國聯邦存款保險公司（the "FDIC"）透過存款保險基金（the "DIF"）提供保險。請參閱本年度10-K申報表所附的Exhibit 21，以取得截至2026年2月15日第五第三銀行控股公司的子公司名單。
有關第五第三銀行控股公司業務的額外資訊，請參閱本年度10-K申報表的第7項。

第五第三銀行控股公司，主要透過第五第三銀行，於其主要地理市場及選定的全國市場中競爭存款、貸款及其他銀行服務。除了銀行機構外，第五第三銀行控股公司還與證券經紀商、股票經紀人、房貸經紀人、投資顧問、專業金融、私人信貸、金融科技及保險公司競爭。這些公司跨地理區域競爭，並為客戶提供傳統銀行服務的有意義替代方案。日益激烈的競爭環境主要歸因於規則的變更、科技的進步、產品交付系統的改變及金融服務提供者的合併速度加快。這些競爭趨勢可能持續下去。

第五第三銀行控股公司的員工資本策略旨在吸引、培訓及保留人才。此策略確保第五第三銀行擁有足夠的人才、能力及組織架構，以支持目前及未來的業務需求。截至2025年12月31日，第五第三銀行控股公司擁有18,676名全職等效員工，與截至2024年12月31日的18,616名員工相比。這些員工透過落實其價值觀，即追求卓越、建立聯繫及展現創意與勇氣，來支持組織的願景與使命。第五第三銀行致力於實踐其價值觀，服務客戶，實現財務表現，並被視為建立吸引人的工作環境的領導者。
第五第三銀行認為，一個投入的員工是其持續成功最重要的資產之一。第五第三銀行控股公司的持續聆聽策略是其包容文化的重要組成部分，透過多種方法提供整體的員工意見收集、衡量與回應方式，以提升員工在職涯關鍵階段的體驗。第五第三銀行控股公司聆聽策略的基礎為員工觀點調查，其中包括與投入、包容、福祉、員工期望及其意圖離職相關的問題。
第五第三銀行控股公司的學習、發展與職涯流動性策略提供個人化且易於接觸的體驗，以促進職涯成長並幫助保留人才。根據員工意見，第五第三銀行持續著重於職涯流動性，並提供增強的工具以支持內部職涯規劃。這包括涵蓋多個領域的強大學習資源組合，包括領導力與專業發展，以促進員工羣體的學習與職涯進步。在2025年，員工參與了超過550,000小時的自發性學習。
2025 年，第五第三銀行推出一個全面的平台，旨在為各層級的領導者提供領導力發展的內容與體驗。幾項新的發展方案已啟動，包括生成式人工智慧（"AI"）培訓、管理者的溝通技巧培訓，以及針對性強化組織內專業與領導能力的方案。第五第三銀行的領導者參與了超過 3,200 種不同的發展體驗。

總報酬 – 薪資與福利
The Bancorp 認識到獎勵員工其才能與對卓越的承諾的重要性。為反映此點，員工的總報酬方案包括具有競爭力的薪資以及完整的福利方案，以支持員工在其職業與生活各階段。
The Bancorp 承諾提供具有競爭力的薪資方案，以吸引與留住頂尖人才，同時推動業務策略並有效管理風險。第五第三銀行的薪資方案設計用以獎勵績效，並符合監管期待，同時反映 The Bancorp 的價值觀與行為準則。The Bancorp 的薪資哲學以創造長期股東價值為中心。
第五第三銀行致力於員工整體的福祉。福利方案設計用以應對員工及其家屬的個人與專業需求。除了傳統的福利方案，The Bancorp 提供全面的支援，包含專注於員工財務、身體、情緒與社會福祉的獨特方案。

paragraphs: 以下為管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析（MD&A），說明影響第五第三銀行公司（"Bancorp" 或 "Fifth Third"）財務狀況與營運成果之重大因素，這些因素包含於合併財務報表期間內，為本檔之組成部分。提及Bancorp時，包含母公司持有公司與所有合併子公司。Bancorp之銀行子公司稱為銀行。

本MD&A概要說明Bancorp財務結果之重點資訊，可能未包含對您而言重要之全部資訊。為更完整了解趨勢、事件、承諾、不確定性、流動性、資本資源與關鍵會計政策與估計，應仔細閱讀本檔全部內容。這些項目均可能影響Bancorp之財務狀況、營運成果與現金流。此外，請參閱本報告之縮寫與縮寫詞彙表，以取得包含於本年度10-K報告中之術語清單，作為讀者理解本年度報告之工具。該縮寫與縮寫詞彙表中所識別之縮寫與縮寫詞彙，於本MD&A、合併財務報表與合併財務報表附註中均有使用。
淨利息收入、淨利息邊際、淨利息差與效率比率於MD&A中以FTE基礎呈現。FTE基礎調整因某些貸款與租賃及證券之收入享有稅務優惠，而這些證券對聯邦所得稅而言並非課稅項目。Bancorp認為此呈現方式為業界偏好的淨利息收入衡量標準，因其提供可比較之課稅與非課稅金額。以FTE基礎呈現淨利息收入為非GAAP衡量指標。如需進一步資訊，請參閱MD&A中之非GAAP財務指標部分。
Bancorp之收入依賴淨利息收入與非利息收入。於2025年12月31日財務年度，以FTE基礎計算之淨利息收入與非利息收入分別佔總收入之66%與34%。Bancorp之主要收入來自美國，客戶為美國居民。利率變動、信用品質、總體經濟趨勢與資本市場為影響Bancorp表現之主要因素。如後續於MD&A之風險管理部分所述，風險識別、衡量、監測、控制與報告對風險管理與財務表現與資本強度為重要。

淨利息收入為資產（如貸款、租賃與證券）所產生之利息收入與負債（如存款、其他短期借款與長期債務）所產生之利息支出之差額。淨利息收入受總體利率水準、短期與長期利率相對水準、利率變動以及利息收入資產與利息負債金額與組成之變動影響。通常，Bancorp於資產上所賺取之利率與於負債上所支付之利率為一段期間內確定。時間經過時，市場利率之變動使Bancorp面臨利率風險，可能對淨利息收入與財務狀況造成不利影響。Bancorp透過持續分析與調整資產與負債組成，根據其付款流、利率、到期時間與對市場利率變動之敏感度來管理此風險。此外，在日常營運過程中，Bancorp會進行某些衍生交易，作為整體策略之一環，以管理其利率與預付款風險。Bancorp亦因借款人信用事件（如貸款違約與擔保不足）所導致之預期現金流變動，而面臨貸款與租賃組合之損失風險。
非利息收入來自財富與資產管理收入、商業付款收入、消費者銀行收入、資本市場費用、商業銀行收入、房貸銀行淨收入、其他非利息收入與證券淨損益。非利息費用包含薪資與福利、資訊科技與通訊、淨營運費用、設備費用、貸款與租賃費用、行銷費用、卡片與處理費用及其他非利息費用。
2026年2月1日，第五第三銀行公司完成與Comerica Incorporated（"Comerica"）之合併，以全股票交易方式進行，價值約127億美元。根據合併協議條款，每持有Comerica普通股一股，可換取1.8663股第五第三銀行公司普通股；每持有Comerica優先股一股，可換取一張新發行之優先股，其條款與Comerica原有優先股相當。
如需更多資訊，請參閱合併財務報表附註之第32項附註。
於 2025 年 9 月 30 日，本公司贖回其 4.500% 固定利率重設累積永續優先股，系列 L，共 14,000 張現行流通股，以及對應的託管股份，依其條款與條件辦理。於贖回前，系列 L 優先股的股息率設定為達成其第一個股息重設日，屆時股息將重設為五年期美國國庫券利率加 4.215%。
有關更多資訊，請參閱財務會計彙編附註第 24 項。48 第五第三銀行控股公司

於 2025 年 6 月 13 日，本銀行公司的董事會授權管理階層透過公開市場或任何私人交易購入 100 百萬股本銀行公司的普通股。此授權取代了 2019 年 6 月的先前授權，且未包含特定目標或到期日。

headings: 信用品質惡化已對 Fifth Third 過去造成負面影響，未來亦可能對 Fifth Third 造成負面影響。
其他金融機構所遭遇的問題可能對金融市場產生普遍性負面影響，並對 Fifth Third 產生直接與間接的負面影響。
無法在公開或私人資本市場進行再融資可能導致違約，進而影響 Fifth Third 的借款人。
Fifth Third 必須維持充足的資金來源與流動性。
Fifth Third 及/或其證券持有人可能因評級機構給予不利評級而受到負面影響。
若 Fifth Third 無法維持或增加其存款，可能會面臨更高的資金成本。
The Bancorp 從其子公司獲取紅利的能力佔其營收的絕大部分，此能力可能影響其流動性及支付紅利的能力。
Fifth Third 可能無法成功實施未來資訊科技系統的升級，這可能會對 Fifth Third 的業務運作及獲利能力產生負面影響。
新興科技進展，例如人工智能，可能使第五第三銀行面臨額外風險。
第五第三銀行可能因詐欺、竊盜或暴力事件而遭受損失。
第五第三銀行若未能吸引並留住具專業技能的人員，可能會遭受影響。
第五第三銀行需面對廣泛的政府管制，這可能會對第五第三銀行或其從事的業務造成不利影響。
第五第三銀行可能因智慧財產權遭未經授權使用而遭受損失。
第五第三銀行需遵守多種監管要求，這些要求可能限制其營運及潛在成長。
針對銀行收取的存款保險費率可能提高。
若觸發對系統重要性金融控股公司或非銀行金融公司的有序清算，第五第三銀行可能需為有序清算基金負擔費用。
美國經濟表現不佳，包括第五第三銀行所服務的地理區域，已對第五第三銀行造成負面影響，未來亦可能造成負面影響。
全球及國內政治、社會、經濟與公共衛生的不確定性與變動，可能對第五第三銀行造成負面影響。
利率的變動可能影響第五第三銀行的營業收入與現金流。
資本市場的變化與趨勢可能影響第五第三銀行的營業收入與現金流。
第五第三銀行的股票價格波動性較高。
市場的變化可能影響第五第三銀行的房貸業務。
若第五第三銀行未能回應金融服務業激烈的競爭與快速變動，或未能適應客戶偏好的改變，其財務表現可能受到影響。
paragraphs: 下列所列之風險與不確定性可能對 Bancorp 之業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大影響。部分風險與不確定性彼此相關，其中一項或數項之發生可能加劇其他風險與不確定性之影響。下列所列之風險與不確定性並非 Fifth Third 所面臨之唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前 Fifth Third 並未知悉，或目前認為不重要，亦可能對其業務造成不利影響。請參閱第 19 頁有關前瞻性陳述之警示資訊。

當 Fifth Third 提供貸款或承諾提供貸款時，Bancorp 會面臨信用風險，即借款人未能償還貸款、租賃、信用卡、衍生性義務或其他信用義務時所產生之損失風險。這些信用組合之表現會顯著影響 Bancorp 之財務結果與財務狀況，包括信用損失之水準與信用損失備抵準備金。若 Fifth Third 之貸款集中於個別借款人、從事相同或類似活動、產業或地理區域之借款人，或一羣借款人可能因經濟或市場條件而獨特或不成比例地受到影響，則其信用風險與信用損失可能增加。請參閱本年報第 7 項「風險管理」部分之「信用風險管理」子節，以取得有關特定集中風險之更多資訊。

Fifth Third 透過對應損失備抵準備金之費用計提，為預期信用損失做備抵。此備抵金額係根據 Fifth Third 對信用組閤中預期將產生之信用損失之評估，包括未資金承諾，並需要對環境做出困難、主觀且複雜的判斷，包括對經濟或市場條件之分析，這些條件可能影響借款人償還貸款之能力。Fifth Third 可能低估其組閤中預期將產生之信用損失，並導致信用損失高於備抵金額。另一方面，Fifth Third 可能因經濟或市場條件之變動，包括通貨膨脹、利率波動、失業率上升或其他因素，如信用協議中保護措施之變動或借款人行為之變化，而提高備抵金額。Fifth Third 相信截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，其 ALLL 以及未資金承諾備抵準備金足以覆蓋預期損失。然而，無法保證這些備抵金額足以覆蓋截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日所存在之所有潛在未來信用損失，特別是在經濟條件惡化的情況下。

Fifth Third 會與金融服務業及其他產業之交易對手有接觸，並常規執行交易，這可能使其在交易對手或客戶違約時面臨信用風險。此外，Fifth Third 之信用風險可能因所持有之擔保品無法實現或以不足以回收貸款或衍生性風險之價格進行清算而受到影響。許多金融機構之商業健全性可能因機構間之信用、交易、結算或其他關係而密切相關。因此，對某機構之擔憂，或該機構違約或威脅違約，可能導致其他機構出現廣泛市場流動性與信用問題、損失或違約。這種情況有時被稱為系統性風險，可能對 Bancorp 日常互動之金融中介機構，如結算機構、結算所、銀行、證券公司與交易所，造成不利影響，因此可能對 Fifth Third 產生不利影響。
部分 Fifth Third 之客戶依賴來自 Bancorp 以外之其他資金來源。若這些借款人無法透過公開或私人資本市場取得資金以進行再融資，則這些借款人可能會出現資金缺口，導致其無法履行對 Bancorp 之短期及/或長期義務。

Fifth Third 必須在業務正常運作中維持足夠之資金來源，以支持其業務運作及償付現有負債，並符合監管機構之期待。Fifth Third 主要依賴銀行存款作為貸款及業務運作之低成本且穩定之資金來源。核心存款，包括交易存款及面額 $250,000 或以下之存款憑證，歷來為 Fifth Third 提供相當規模之相對穩定且低成本資金（截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之年度，核心存款平均資助了總資產平均值的 77%）。除了客戶存款外，流動性來源還包括證券投資組合、Fifth Third 在二級市場出售或證券化貸款、將貸款及投資證券質押以取得 FHLB 與 FRB 之擔保融資、以及 Fifth Third 在貨幣市場與資本市場籌集資金之能力。
